title: The Zodiac Killer's 340 cipher — cracked after 51 years
sources: Wikipedia: Zodiac Killer — an unidentified serial killer who attacked seven people on four occasions in the San Francisco Bay Area between December 1968 and October 1969; five died, two survived; three couples (Lake Herman Road, Blue Rock Springs, Lake Berryessa) and the cab driver Paul Stine in Presidio Heights; from 1969 to 1974 he sent over twenty letters to newspapers, signed with a crosshair-like symbol; the Z408 cipher, mailed in three parts on 31 July 1969 with a demand to print it on the front page, was cracked on 5 August 1969 by Donald and Bettye Harden of Salinas, neither a cryptologist — it spoke of killing and of victims becoming his slaves in the afterlife; the Z340 cipher (8 November 1969) stayed unsolved for 51 years until 5 December 2020, when David Oranchak (US), Sam Blake (Australia) and Jarl Van Eycke (Belgium) ran 650,000 possible solutions through Van Eycke's AZdecrypt; the FBI verified it; the message begins 'I hope you are having lots of fun in trying to catch me' and says he is not afraid of the gas chamber 'because it will send me to paradice all the sooner'; it gives no clue to his identity; the only suspect police named was Arthur Leigh Allen, who died in 1992; the short Z13 ('My name is…') and Z32 ciphers remain unsolved.
Images (public domain, Wikimedia Commons): Zodiac letters and ciphers (1969–1970), the SFPD composite sketch (1969), Lake Berryessa
Archive film (public domain): Caltrans Photolog (California state highways); 'Rolling Stones at Altamont' (Bay Area, December 1969); 'Tidningstryck' (newspaper printing, 1937) — illustrative
Music: Beethoven, Moonlight Sonata, 1st movement, public domain

post.facebook:
In 1969, a killer mailed a secret code to a San Francisco newspaper. It took 51 years to crack it.

He called himself the Zodiac. In less than a year he attacked seven people around San Francisco Bay; five died. Then came the letters, signed with a crosshair, demanding to be printed on the front page. His first cipher was cracked within days by an ordinary couple in Salinas. The second — 340 symbols — beat everyone who tried for half a century.

In December 2020, three amateurs in America, Australia and Belgium ran 650,000 possible keys through a computer, and it cracked. The FBI confirmed it. The first line: "I hope you are having lots of fun in trying to catch me." He wasn't afraid of the gas chamber, he wrote, because it would send him to paradise all the sooner.

But no name. The only suspect police ever named, Arthur Leigh Allen, died in 1992, never charged. Two of the Zodiac's ciphers are still unsolved — and one begins "My name is…" 👇

youtube.description:
In 1969, a killer mailed a secret code to a San Francisco newspaper. It took 51 years to crack it.

The Zodiac Killer attacked seven people around San Francisco Bay in 1968–69 and taunted police with letters and ciphers. His 408-symbol cipher was solved within days by a couple in Salinas; his 340-symbol cipher (Z340) stayed unsolved until December 2020, when David Oranchak, Sam Blake and Jarl Van Eycke cracked it — the FBI confirmed the solution. It reveals no name. The only suspect police named, Arthur Leigh Allen, died in 1992, and two of the Zodiac's ciphers, including the one that begins "My name is", are still unsolved.
